model_interpretation.claim: For large n, a separate output-zeroing launch followed by one grid-stride reduction launch should reduce launch and scratch-stage overhead versus the existing hierarchy. The tradeoff is one contended int32 atomic per CTA; using 256-thread CTAs, a target of 2048 elements per CTA, and a 1024-CTA cap tests whether this keeps input parallelism high enough without excessive aggregation contention. This remains an unmeasured hypothesis.

items.subject: Large-input atomic final aggregation
items.objective: In src/candidate.cu, evaluate a large-input alternative with an ordered output-zeroing kernel followed by a multi-CTA grid-stride reduction; each CTA reduces its own values and performs one int32 atomicAdd to out. Tune CTA count/work per CTA to balance input throughput against contention. Do not rely on initialized scratch or unsafe inter-block initialization. Preserve exact results, bounds, ABI, default-stream ordering, and a correct fallback for other legal sizes; compare all checks and repeated timings against the baseline and hierarchical approach.
